explanation: The pole fires where the text names, titles or identifies a particular referent rather than merely describing it: on a naming/attribution predicate (called, known as, dubbed, nicknamed, termed, regarded as, referred to as, considered, described as, Chinese 被称为/称为) applied to a specific entity, and on the equative copula 'X is the Y' that equates a specific entity with a definite title, role or superlative ('Paris is the capital of France', 'Real estate is the main engine of China's economic growth', 'the world's oldest animal cave painting'); it peaks on the naming predicate itself (' called', ' nicknamed', ' as', ' considered') and on the determiner that opens the designation (' the Y'), and the zero-copula counterparts behave the same way (Chinese nominal-predicate bios 'X（），男，…，中国财政学家', German 'die Quirquinchos genannt'). It stays near zero on ascriptive predication ('X is a city / large / beautiful / used to…'), on class-membership definitions and technical name-giving for a kind or an indefinite subject ('A dog is a domesticated descendant of the wolf', 'The tool is called a hammer', 'In mathematics, this object is called a group', 'This pattern of cracking is referred to as the fatigue limit'), on naming applied to a generic or abstract subject ('The region is called paradise on earth', 'This place is called…'), on determiners outside predicate position ('The dog chased the cat around the garden' — 0.00 of max) and on ordinary verb phrases.
